title: Conjecture 1 (Nadjafi-Arani, Khodashenas, and Ashrafi, 2012)
statement_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph and let $B_1, \ldots, B_k$ be all its non-complete blocks of respective orders $n_1, \ldots, n_k$. Then $$\eta(G) \geq \sum_{i=1}^{k}(2n_i - 6).$$
context_text: Nadjafi-Arani et al. investigated properties of $\eta(G) = \mathrm{Sz}(G) - W(G)$ and proposed this lower bound in terms of the non-complete blocks of a graph. The conjecture generalises the 2-connected case and is the central result the paper sets out to prove.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture in full: first Theorem 2 establishes $\eta(G) \geq 2n-6$ for every 2-connected non-complete graph on $n$ vertices, and Corollary 3 then derives the general block-sum bound as a direct consequence.
paper_title: On the difference between the Szeged and Wiener index

title: Conjecture 5
statement_text: Let $G$ be a 2-connected graph of order $n \geq 10$ not isomorphic to $K_n$, $K^2_n$, or $K^{n-2}_n$. Then $\eta(G) \geq 2n$.
context_text: Graphs are simple. The Wiener index is $W(G)=\sum_{\{a,b\}\subseteq V}d(a,b)$, the sum of distances over all pairs of vertices, and the Szeged index is $\mathrm{Sz}(G)=\sum_{ab\in E}n_{ab}(a)\,n_{ab}(b)$, where $n_{ab}(a)$ is the number of vertices strictly closer to $a$ than to $b$. Let $\eta(G)=\mathrm{Sz}(G)-W(G)$; it is non-negative for connected graphs, with equality exactly for block graphs. For $2\le t\le n-2$, $K_n^t$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n-1}$ by adding a new vertex adjacent to $t$ of the old vertices (it is $2$-connected and non-complete). The authors prove that every $2$-connected non-complete graph on $n$ vertices has $\eta(G)\ge2n-6$ (which implies the conjecture of Nadjafi-Arani, Khodashenas and Ashrafi that $\eta(G)\ge\sum_i(2n_i-6)$ over the non-complete blocks of orders $n_i$), and $\eta(G)\ge2n-5$ unless $G$ is $K_n^2$ or $K_n^{n-2}$. Since $\eta(K_n)=0$ and $\eta(K_n^2)=\eta(K_n^{n-2})=2n-6$, and a computer search found $2$-connected graphs with $\eta(G)<2n$ only on at most $9$ vertices (none on $10$ vertices), they conjecture this stronger bound.
paper_title: On the difference between the Szeged and Wiener index
